purpose: Descriptive mechanism evidence from existing full-source EC aggregates; distinguish recovered legal alternatives from mere malformed-output repair.
interpretation: Both arms have valid EC output on all 128 sources and share the public interface. The learned-library gain therefore cannot be explained solely by fixing malformed JSON. Existing complete-claim counts show substantially more recovered legal alternatives and fewer erroneous predictions.
limits: Counts are descriptive pooled claim totals, not the source-mean native F1 or a new significance test.
This comparison establishes utility of the actual learned library under the shared input conditions, not the isolated causal contribution of a single edit or objective.
Shared prerequisites and answer-space assistance still define the task; these counts do not demonstrate official Advanced or end-to-end performance.
